# ISSUE-74 implementation plan

Project body dependencies into GitHub blocked-by relationships and explicitly order published children. Keep WorkUnit parsing, approval, claim eligibility, and selection algorithms unchanged. This refresh targets the operator-specified approved main base `454a64b`. It is a planning artifact only. The pending organization-fork PR is independent: do not merge it, wait for it, or rely on its symbols. Keep necessary shared-file edits narrow and place new feature code and tests in focused package files.

Revisions R1/R2: existing `LinkSubIssue` failures and approval skipping remain unchanged; only the new blocked-by and priority operations are advisory. Adapter idempotence uses database IDs, and lint uses repository-qualified identities.

## Dimensions

Advisory: size `multi_area`, uncertainty `unknown` (external API contract unavailable here), risk `standard`. No execution profile is selected. Estimated implementation and verification: 8–12 hours, within the 16-hour total claim budget.

## What we know

- `internal/tracker/tracker.go:136` defines the tracker interface; native hierarchy methods already exist at lines 148–150. `Issue` has no database ID or explicit repository field (`tracker.go:9`), but has `HTMLURL`; `ghIssueResponse.ID` exists (`github.go:235`). Resolve IDs inside the GitHub adapter rather than adding persisted fields.
- `internal/tracker/github.go:370` paginates native sub-issues; `LinkSubIssue` at line 393 resolves the child's database ID and checks existing parent membership before POST. Its payload is `sub_issue_id`, not an issue number. The fake HTTP fixture in `github_test.go:209` tests this distinction.
- `internal/cli/issue.go:30` creates a formatted WorkUnit, then links its parent and optionally approves it. Lint at line 164 parses the body and emits dimension advice and JSON. Decomposition command begins at line 280.
- `internal/workflow/engine.go:652` implements `DecomposeIssue`; sequential dependencies are resolved before issue creation. Currently a hierarchy-link error is fatal and the child is appended only after linking, losing it from the returned list on failure.
- `internal/workflow/project_plan.go:1045` implements `applyRoadmapEpicAndChildren`; lines 1295–1353 map roadmap steps to actual issue numbers and create/reuse children. Both reused and new children must receive projection attempts. Existing body/hash preflight must remain intact.
- `internal/lease/manager.go:295` verifies only `wu.DependsOn`, fetching prerequisite issue state. No native dependency API participates. `internal/cli/selection.go:438` already reads native sibling order; preserve that algorithm and its tests unchanged.
- `internal/tracker/local.go:24` defines persisted `localState`, including existing `ChildOrder`. New display-only methods need no schema additions.
- `internal/cli/issue.go:68–79` returns hierarchy errors before approval; `internal/workflow/project_plan.go:1341–1346` does the same. `TestRunProjectPlanValidationIdempotencyConflictsAndRetry` (`project_plan_test.go:329–350`) requires a fatal partial hierarchy failure followed by reuse on retry. Preserve this regression unchanged.
- `Makefile:44` runs lint, race tests, and changelog-check; lint includes formatting, vet, and staticcheck. `Makefile:60` checks unreleased fragments with `go run ./cmd/changelog --check`. Approved policy additionally requires `go build ./...` and `go test ./...`.
- Repository source does not yet implement dependency or priority endpoints. Wire keys below are retained design assumptions, awaiting primary-reference verification.
- `internal/workflow/dependencies.go:1` and `dependencies_test.go` already implement agent dependency-cache preparation, an unrelated feature. Preserve both unchanged; use `native_projection.go` for this feature.
- This sandbox exposes a source snapshot without `.git`; `git rev-parse HEAD` fails. Therefore `454a64b` is the operator-specified target, not an independently verified checkout identity. All line references were refreshed against the supplied snapshot where relevant.

## What we're assuming

- Expected REST routes are GET/POST `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/dependencies/blocked_by` and PATCH `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/sub_issues/priority`, the latter carrying `sub_issue_id` and one anchor. These are proposed API shapes, not independently verified facts in this run.
- Expected fine-grained permission is Issues read for listing and Issues write for mutations, compatible with existing creation/linking credentials. Confirm actor requirements and token types from official endpoint documentation before claiming this in product docs. Do not change token scopes, permission admission, or workflows.
- Rerun idempotency concerns relationship creation and roadmap reuse. `issue create` and decomposition currently create new issues on another invocation; adding global issue-creation deduplication is outside scope.

## Open questions

Official references: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/issue-dependencies and https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/sub-issues . Both curl requests failed with `Could not resolve host: docs.github.com`; no independent API-doc verification was possible. At implementation step 1, inspect the official docs or a supplied official OpenAPI snapshot for exact verbs, payloads, response status/body, pagination, supported token permissions, and duplicate/validation errors. Keep those details unverified until evidence is recorded. Fake REST tests can be developed in the sandbox; live service evidence belongs in operator review and must not block sandbox acceptance.

Does GitHub return a distinguishable already-present error? Avoid depending on its wording: pre-list relationships, and after a potentially duplicate conflict/validation response re-list and accept success only when the exact relationship now exists. Unrelated 422, permission, missing issue, cycle/limit, and transport failures remain errors for the caller to warn about. Confirm which statuses permit this reconciliation from docs/source; never blanket-swallow 422.

If the docs require additional permission, document it and retain graceful warnings under current credentials. Reopen for a maintainer decision if meeting acceptance would require expanding credentials or changing authorization. No live API requirement may be added to the implementation gate.

## Design and exact touchpoints

Exact new files (each absent in the supplied snapshot by explicit path existence checks):

- `internal/tracker/github_dependencies.go`: all NEW GitHub dependency and priority methods, private wire response structs, ID/identity decoding, pagination, and reconciliation helpers. Reuse existing `GitHubTracker`, `ghIssueResponse`, and REST client without appending methods to `github.go`.
- `internal/tracker/github_dependencies_test.go`: all new adapter HTTP cases; reuse `newHTTPGitHubTracker` from existing package tests without adding feature tests to `github_test.go`.
- `internal/tracker/local_dependencies.go` and `internal/tracker/local_dependencies_test.go`: local no-op methods and byte-for-byte storage compatibility coverage.
- `internal/workflow/native_projection.go` and `internal/workflow/native_projection_test.go`: dependency projection/warning helpers and new decomposition/roadmap projection, ordering, and R1 regressions.
- `internal/cli/issue_dependencies.go` and `internal/cli/issue_dependencies_test.go`: qualified lint drift helper and feature-specific create/decompose/roadmap/lint CLI tests, including stderr and JSON.
- `internal/lease/native_projection_test.go`: body-only enforcement and real claim-path regressions; no new lease production code.
- `changes/unreleased/74.md`: concise fragment following the existing fragment format; do not edit aggregate CHANGELOG.md.

All these paths were checked absent with `Path.exists()` in this planning run. There is no Git object database here, so absence at the approved commit remains unverified. In a coordinator checkout, verify each exact path using `git cat-file -e 454a64b:<path>` (nonzero means absent only after `git rev-parse --verify 454a64b^{commit}` succeeds). If a path exists at that base, classify it as modified and reconcile its contents; never overwrite existing content as a new file. This provenance check is separate from implementation's fake-API acceptance and introduces no dependency on the org-fork PR.

Existing files to modify only where required:

- `internal/tracker/tracker.go`: extend `Tracker` with `ListBlockedBy(ctx, issueNumber) ([]BlockedByReference, error)`, `LinkBlockedBy(ctx, issueNumber, prerequisiteNumber) error`, and `OrderSubIssues(ctx, parentNumber, childNumbers []int) error`. Define an ephemeral `BlockedByReference` value with repository owner/name, number, and HTML URL (not persisted in Issue/localState). Document projection-only meaning. No removal/sync API.
- `internal/tracker/github_dependencies.go` (new): implement these methods using RESTClient and existing response types; keep database IDs internal. Decode each native row’s database ID and repository identity (`repository_url` or validated HTML URL); expose its qualified reference for lint. Validate inputs, context, missing IDs, and incomplete identity; never silently assume an unidentified row is local. Paginate blocked-by reads. Resolve the local prerequisite database ID, then compare that ID with every listed row ID before skipping POST. A cross-repository issue with the same number must not suppress linking. Reconcile ambiguous duplicate failures against a fresh paginated read by the same exact database ID, preserving wrapped errors otherwise. Deduplicate repeated body dependency numbers; projection and lint ignore self-dependencies using the created/existing issue number, matching VerifyDependencies without editing the body.
- Priority ordering: resolve child database IDs and list current siblings. For two or more desired children, move the first before the second with `before_id`, then each subsequent child after the preceding child with `after_id`. Send exactly one anchor per mutation. Empty/singleton lists require no relative move. Preserve unrelated siblings and never detach or reparent children. Existing LinkSubIssue failure returns immediately and never reaches ordering. If priority’s own membership lookup fails or observes missing membership after successful hierarchy linking, return a priority error for the caller to warn about; never reparent or change hierarchy failure handling. Repeat application converges to the same requested relative order.
- `internal/tracker/local_dependencies.go` (new): new methods return empty projection/nil success without persisting data or mutating existing hierarchy/order. Callers skip drift comparison for local backend to avoid warnings for intentionally unsupported native projections. Do not add dependency fields to localState.
- `internal/cli/issue.go`: after successful create, attempt every body dependency and emit contextual warnings via `cmd.ErrOrStderr()` while retaining normal text/JSON issue output. Preserve the existing fatal hierarchy-link branch, exact error message, and its position before --ready approval. Only ListBlockedBy/LinkBlockedBy and OrderSubIssues errors are advisory; preserve real create/validation/approval failures. Lint derives the current repository identity from the fetched issue HTMLURL (validated against configured repository context) and qualifies body numbers with that identity and compares these references with all paginated native links, emits deterministic missing/extra warnings in text and additive `warnings` JSON, keeps `status: valid`, and returns success. Cross-repository links are extras displayed as full owner/repo#number references; they never satisfy local dependencies. For body [7] and native [other/repo#7], emit both missing current/repo#7 and extra other/repo#7. Sort/deduplicate by qualified identity, not number. A native read or identity-resolution failure yields an unavailable-check warning, not fabricated drift. No lint writes.
- `internal/workflow/engine.go`: extend `DecomposeIssue` with an optional warning callback (variadic to preserve current call sites); retain the existing create/LinkSubIssue/append sequence, fatal hierarchy errors, and exact messages. After successful hierarchy linking, attempt every dependency projection; warn and continue only for new blocked-by failures, retain authored/resolved body, and order collected children after a successful creation loop. OrderSubIssues failures are advisory. Do not continue the loop after a hierarchy failure. `newDecomposeCmd` supplies stderr callback; default callers remain compatible.
- `internal/workflow/project_plan.go`: add additive `Warnings []string` to `ProjectPlanReport`; accumulate projection/order warnings while retaining created/existing issue results. Apply dependency projection to both reuse and creation branches after existing body validation and successful hierarchy linking. For reused children, parse depends_on from childIss.Body, the authoritative existing body, rather than the re-mapped in-memory u.DependsOn. Skip self-reference with childIss.Number. Preserve both existing fatal LinkSubIssue branches and messages, including the new-child branch before Ready approval; return immediately on hierarchy failure without approving that child. Order children in roadmap file order after the successful loop. Never modify preflight hashes, dependency mapping, approval rules, leftovers, or scan behavior.
- `internal/cli/plan.go`: print collected warnings to stderr before normal report rendering/export so machine-readable output remains parseable. No global logging or engine writes to process stderr.
- Put new feature tests exclusively in the focused test files above. Reuse existing package fixtures. Change existing fixture handlers only if the new requests require it, with no unrelated test additions or refactors. Preserve existing hierarchy failure assertions in place. `github.go` and `github_test.go` are expected unchanged; if a shared fixture there truly needs adaptation, limit it to the required handler branch and explain why in the diff.
- Update existing `docs/project.md` (create/decompose), `docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md` (epic publishing), `docs/GITHUB.md` (verified API permissions), and `docs/developer.md` (dependency creation and lint drift). Explain native display, warnings, retry behavior, and body authority in ordinary developer language. Existing edit semantics remain unchanged; do not promise later-edit synchronization.

Existing production touchpoints are limited to `internal/tracker/tracker.go`, `internal/cli/issue.go`, `internal/cli/plan.go`, `internal/workflow/engine.go`, and `internal/workflow/project_plan.go`. Helper bodies belong in the new files above; existing entry points receive only required calls/signature/report changes. No edits to organization-fork verification, token handling, or shared GitHub response conversion are planned.

## Implementation sequence

1. Refresh exact symbols/line numbers against the supplied approved-base snapshot and inspect official API docs/source as above. Verify base/path provenance where Git metadata is available; proceed independently of the pending org-fork PR. Record confirmed contract and permission facts; adapt wire details without expanding scope.
2. Extend tracker interface, GitHub adapter, and local no-op methods together. Add fake REST tests for IDs, pagination, repeated/racing link creation, priority anchors, and errors.
3. Wire creation/decomposition/roadmap projection and explicit ordering. Collect warnings with issue numbers/URLs and operation context; keep stdout results and body dependency bytes intact. Continue remaining projection operations after an independent blocked-by/priority API failure only. Existing hierarchy failures still return immediately and skip approval.
4. Add read-only lint drift comparison, deterministic text/JSON warning output, and local skip behavior.
5. Add body-only VerifyDependencies and actual claim-path regressions without changing enforcement code. Preserve selection implementation and regression suite.
6. Update scoped docs using confirmed API permissions, run focused tests and required full checks, and provide the optional live operator checklist separately.

## HANDOFF

This artifact is evidence to check against source, not authority over approved inputs, gates, or validation.

Entry points: `internal/tracker/tracker.go:136`, `internal/tracker/github.go:370`, `internal/tracker/local.go:24`, `internal/cli/issue.go:30`, `internal/cli/issue.go:164`, `internal/cli/issue.go:280`, `internal/workflow/engine.go:652`, `internal/workflow/project_plan.go:66`, `internal/workflow/project_plan.go:1045`, `internal/cli/plan.go:72`, and `internal/lease/manager.go:295`.

Existing fixtures: `newHTTPGitHubTracker` and `TestGitHubTrackerEpicIssueTypeAndNativeSubIssues` (`github_test.go:209`), `TestCollaborativeHandoffAndDecomposition` (`engine_test.go:210`), `flakyLinkTracker` (`project_plan_test.go:77`), `TestRunProjectPlanValidationIdempotencyConflictsAndRetry` (`project_plan_test.go:240`), existing CLI GitHub creation fixtures (`issue_allow_harness_test.go:416`), lease manager claim setup helpers, and selection fixtures (`selection_test.go:41`). Extend their handlers for new read/write requests rather than hiding unexpected requests.

Focused verification commands:

```bash
go test ./internal/tracker
go test ./internal/workflow -run 'Test(CollaborativeHandoffAndDecomposition|RunProjectPlan|NativeProjection)'
go test ./internal/cli -run 'Test(Issue|CLI.*(Create|Lint|Decompose|Plan)|NativeProjection)'
go test ./internal/lease -run 'Test(NativeProjection|VerifyDependencies)'
go test ./internal/cli
```

Checked assumptions: source confirms resolved dependency timing, roadmap reuse, database-ID availability, and body-only enforcement. REST payload details beyond existing hierarchy linkage and operator-provided keys remain unverified; no live calls were made. See TEST_PLAN.md for all acceptance checks.

Reopen if API contract needs new authority, token scopes, protected files, later-edit synchronization, global creation deduplication, or selection changes; recommend follow-up work rather than widening this issue. Reopen if a verified base differs materially from this snapshot, a chosen focused file already has incompatible content, or the work no longer fits the claim budget. Resolve only actual shared-file conflicts; do not make merging the org-fork PR a plan step.

### What this change breaks

- Existing fatal hierarchy-link expectations in `project_plan_test.go` (`flakyLinkTracker`, TestRunProjectPlanValidationIdempotencyConflictsAndRetry, including its existing failure/retry assertions): preserve unchanged. Preserve related CLI/decomposition errors and messages unchanged. Add separate regressions for hierarchy failure skipping --ready approval; do not rewrite existing tests to accept warnings. Creation, body/hash conflicts, and approval failures remain fatal.
- Existing HTTP handlers in `github_test.go` and `issue_allow_harness_test.go`: preserve unless a newly exercised publishing request requires a minimal fixture branch; put new ID assertions and feature cases in focused test files. Preserve existing native-parent validation tests.
- `Tracker` implementers/test doubles: interface additions require both concrete backends to compile; embedded Tracker doubles inherit methods, explicit implementations must be updated as compile errors identify them. No stored Issue or localState field changes.
- `ProjectPlanReport` serialization tests (`project_plan_test.go:507`): preserve existing output when no warnings via omitempty; add warning serialization checks.
- Docs found by repository search: `docs/project.md:164,180`, `docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:74,137`, `docs/GITHUB.md:256`, `docs/developer.md:127,640` receive scoped wording. Preserve the edit-field description at `docs/developer.md:51`; it does not imply native edit synchronization. README command table at line 250 and WORKFLOWS overview at line 161 remain accurate and are preserved unchanged; protected skill templates and AGENTS.md remain unchanged.
- `internal/cli/selection.go` and `selection_test.go`, WorkUnit formats, edit command, `VerifyDependencies`, security policy, and coordinator state: preserve unchanged. Explicit native order can affect the existing sibling-order input, but no selection behavior or dependency authority is redesigned.

# ISSUE-74 test plan

All automated acceptance uses fake REST or local fixtures. Live GitHub checks are an operator review task, not sandbox acceptance. This planning run inspected source only; tests below are planned, not claimed as passing.

## Acceptance mapping

| Criterion | Concrete coverage | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Create/decompose/roadmap blocked-by projection and idempotency | Fake REST gives prerequisite number 7 database ID 7007; assert POST targets the dependent issue and sends `issue_id: 7007`. Cover multiple/duplicate dependencies, no dependencies, sequential and parallel decomposition, explicit subtask dependencies, roadmap step-number resolution and external prerequisites. Apply roadmap twice: same issues, no duplicate relationships; existing children retry failed projections. Repeat tracker LinkBlockedBy and simulate concurrent creation: paginated read-back confirms the exact prerequisite database ID. Seed other/repo#7 with a different database ID: it must not suppress POST for local #7, either initially or during race reconciliation. Reused roadmap children project dependencies parsed from their existing authoritative body, Verify the source passed to projection is the parsed existing body; retain end-to-end preflight equality/conflict checks unchanged. If a source-distinguishing mismatch fixture is needed, exercise a narrow projection helper directly rather than weakening roadmap preflight. Skip self-reference consistently with VerifyDependencies; body bytes stay unchanged. Do not expect create/decompose invocations to deduplicate issue creation. | `go test ./internal/tracker ./internal/workflow ./internal/cli` |
| 2. Native sub-issue priority order | Fake priority endpoint maintains deliberately shuffled siblings with IDs unequal to issue numbers. Assert PATCH route, `sub_issue_id`, exactly one of `before_id`/`after_id`, final relative order matching requested children, and unchanged unrelated membership. Cover empty/singleton, multiple children, repeat order, reused roadmap children, and priority lookup observing missing membership after successful hierarchy linking. Existing hierarchy POST failures remain fatal and do not reach ordering. Assert both publishing paths invoke priority API rather than relying on creation sequence. | `go test ./internal/tracker ./internal/workflow ./internal/cli` |
| 3. Warning and created result after projection failure | Inject only new dependency GET/POST and priority lookup/PATCH failures after create in each CLI path. Assert stderr warning identifies affected issue/operation; stdout text still names created issues, JSON remains parseable with created issue objects, and projection failures alone return success. Attempt remaining independent dependencies/children. Compare persisted WorkUnit body and DependsOn before/after failures; no rollback, dependency removal, or state authority writes. Preserve hard failures for issue creation, malformed WorkUnits, roadmap preflight conflicts, and actual approval failure. Separate hierarchy regressions in create, decompose, and roadmap assert LinkSubIssue failure still returns an error with the existing message and stops subsequent processing. In create and roadmap with --ready, assert approval of the affected child is skipped; decomposition retains its draft-only behavior. Keep TestRunProjectPlanValidationIdempotencyConflictsAndRetry and its flakyLinkTracker hierarchy-failure/retry assertions unchanged; add new approval-skipping coverage separately. | `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/workflow` |
| 4. Lint missing/extra drift | Body [7,8], native [8,9] yields exactly missing 7 and extra 9 in deterministic text and JSON warnings, status valid and success exit. Qualify body references with the current repository. Body [7] with native [other/repo#7] yields missing current/repo#7 and extra other/repo#7 in both text and JSON, with full unambiguous references; when local #7 is also linked, only the cross-repo extra remains. Put the same-number cross-repo row and the local row on different pages in both orders. Cover matching/empty/duplicate qualified sets, self-reference skipped in both sets to match existing dependency semantics, closed dependencies, paginated lists, and native lookup unavailable (warning, no invented missing set). Assert lint performs GET only and never edits body/native links. Local lint remains warning-free for unsupported projection. Preserve existing schema failure and dimension output. | `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/tracker` |
| 5. Body-only dependency enforcement | Using a tracker double with independently controlled body and native links, native-only open dependency must not block VerifyDependencies or an otherwise eligible claim. Body-listed open prerequisite with absent/removed native link must return ErrDependenciesUnmet and prevent claim; closing it allows claim independently of native projection. Assert claim/VerifyDependencies do not call ListBlockedBy. Reuse manager approval/claim fixtures so unrelated approval gates are satisfied. Existing selection suite stays unchanged. | `go test ./internal/lease ./internal/cli` |
| 6. Local compatibility | Invoke every new method repeatedly against local fixture, expect success/empty native list; compare existing state bytes before/after, reopen tracker, confirm no added fields, parent/order/issue/dependency changes, and no file created when invoking no-ops on a fresh root. Existing hierarchy behavior remains intact. | `go test ./internal/tracker` |
| 7. Fake GitHub coverage and full checks | Put new HTTP cases in `internal/tracker/github_dependencies_test.go`, workflow cases in `internal/workflow/native_projection_test.go`, CLI cases in `internal/cli/issue_dependencies_test.go`, local cases in `internal/tracker/local_dependencies_test.go`, and enforcement cases in `internal/lease/native_projection_test.go`. Use existing httptest RESTClient helpers; all new mutations must be exercised over HTTP, not only method mocks. Cover permissions/errors, IDs, repeat calls, ordering, warnings, and drift. Run full policy checks below after focused tests. | `make check` plus approved checks below |

## REST contract and error cases

Before finalizing endpoint fixtures, verify against the official dependency and sub-issue docs linked in PLAN.md or an official OpenAPI source. Record source revision/date and actual permission/status findings. This sandbox could not resolve docs.github.com; expected routes and permission assumptions are not verification evidence.

Test pagination beyond 100 results, context cancellation, missing/nonpositive database ID, self/invalid inputs, 403, 404, unrelated 422, server/transport failure, and duplicate-race read-back success/failure. Use distinct database IDs for equal issue numbers across repositories. On duplicate-race read-back, cross-repo #7 alone must leave local #7’s failure visible; exact local ID on a later page permits success. Missing or malformed repository identity yields an unavailable-check warning rather than a guessed local identity. Only confirmed presence of the exact relationship by database ID may convert an ambiguous duplicate failure into success. Permission denial remains visible as a warning after creation, never a request for broader credentials. Confirm priority payload contains database IDs and no invented `priority` index or `after` field.

## Separate live operator review

With an operator-owned disposable GitHub repository and existing issue creation/sub-issue credentials, review the confirmed endpoint permission documentation, publish a small roadmap with multiple prerequisites, inspect blocked-by links and child order, and reapply to confirm stable issue identities/relationships/order. Also inspect create and decomposition results. Introduce native drift manually and inspect lint text/JSON. Exercise a permission-limited projection failure if the fixture permits, checking warnings and visible created issues. Record HTTP status/error evidence without tokens. These live checks establish actual account/service behavior; they are not prerequisites to sandbox test acceptance or implementation startup. If docs require extra permission, document the requirement and retain current-credential graceful failure rather than expanding scopes.

## Review boundaries

Verify existing hierarchy-failure regression and messages remain unchanged, with new separate approval-skipping coverage; only new blocked-by/priority failures are advisory. Inspect final diff for unchanged body-only enforcement, selection algorithms, local stored schema, roadmap idempotency hashes, authorization, and protected paths. Confirm new GitHub methods and feature tests are in the declared focused files, shared-file edits are required integration only, and implementation is independent of the organization-fork PR and did not include later-edit sync or unrelated CLI refactoring. Report any official-doc verification still unavailable as an open review item, without claiming it was completed.
